subject_session: all 15 sessions, 5 mice (LA3, LA8, LA9, LA11, LA12); prototyping on sub-LA9_ses-1, decoding headline on sub-LA11_ses-1

headline_stat.name: best-session single-trial decoding accuracy (5 tones, chance 0.20)

stated_limitation: The main limitation is the stimulus set. This dandiset uses five frequencies one octave apart at a single sound level, so tuning *width* cannot be measured with any precision and the curves are five-point samples of what is really a continuous frequency response area. The conclusions here concern the existence, reliability and readability of frequency tuning, not its bandwidth.

justification.dataset: 000986 is a standard mouse auditory-cortex Neuropixels pure-tone dataset, the canonical choice for demonstrating frequency tuning.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile across all 15 sessions with correct trial alignment and mirrored baseline windows, but no spike-sorting quality metrics beyond statistical responsiveness tests.
justification.analysis: Wilcoxon/Kruskal-Wallis with FDR correction plus split-half shuffle control, pre-tone decoding control, and held-out GLM comparison are all appropriate with the required null distributions present.
justification.correctness: Reported values (decoding 0.95, split-half r=0.98, latency 18 ms, GLM deltas) reproduce from the figures and committed CSV, are internally consistent, and rest on very large samples.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show the effect unambiguously, and example units chosen by drive strength are all strongly significant and honestly characterized.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate, the borderline arousal effect and the single-unit GLM exception are disclosed, and a specific stimulus-set limitation is stated plainly.
justification.verdict: The work is sound, well-controlled, and honestly reported; I would take the result and move on.
